info.bio:
Usher Raymond IV, conocido profesionalmente como Usher, es un cantante, compositor de canciones, y actor estadounidense nacido en Dallas, Texas, el 14 de octubre de 1978.

Criado en Atlanta, Georgia, y Chattanooga, Tennessee, Usher soñaba con ser jugador de baloncesto o rugby antes de descubrir su pasión por la música, la misma que le hizo firmar su primer contrato discográfico cuando apenas contaba con 13 años de edad.

En agosto de 1994 debutó en el mundo de la música con Usher

podcast.title: Album Sales (2004)
podcast.body: Usher's album sales in 2004 reached approximately 7 million copies, matching the previous year's top sellers. His commercial success was notable as the music industry grappled with evolving distribution models and declining physical sales. "2004, Oshar with about the same."

podcast.title: Grammy Nominations and Wins (2005)
podcast.body: Usher was nominated eight times at the 2005 Grammys and won three prizes, but all were in R&B genre categories. He controversially lost Record of the Year for his smash hit "Yeah!" to Ray Charles and Nora Jones, an outcome deemed a "pinnacle of avoiding cultural relevance." "Usher was nominated eight times at the Grammys of 2005, and he won three prizes, but only in the R&B genre categories."

podcast.title: Double Self-Replacement at #1
podcast.body: In 2004, Usher's imperial year was highlighted by him replacing himself at number one twice, with singles "Yeah!," "Burn," and "Confessions Part II," and spending over half the year atop the Hot 100, including his duet "My Boo" with Alicia Keys. "Usher's 2004 could not have been more Imperial. He replaced himself at number one twice between the singles Yeah, Burn and Confessions Part 2."

podcast.title: Imperial Phase Ends with Follow-Up Failures
podcast.body: Usher's imperial phase, which reached a peak in 2004 and saw a brief resurgence in 2008 with "Love in This Club," ultimately ended when three straight follow-up singles missed the top 10, with two even missing the top 40. This demonstrated that an imperial phase is a "delicate thing" and not an automatic chart-topper status. "But then three straight Usher follow-up singles missed the top 10, two of them even missed the top 40, and his Imperial Phase was undoubtedly done."

xref.title: Appearance and Impact (2009)
xref.body: This band appeared around 2009, sounding fresh and different. They achieved significant commercial success and had both cross-genre and cross-generational appeal, helping to usher in a new generation of softer and poppier alt rock, and sparking a folk scene growth in Britain. "When they appeared, they sounded fresh and different."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

xref.title: "Blue Monday" Composition & Instrumentation
xref.body: The composition of "Blue Monday" involved a complex setup: a sequencer built by Stephen Morris connected to an Emulator sampler, a Moog Source keyboard for the bass line, and an Oberheim DMX drum machine. Engineer Martin Usher wrote code to synchronize these devices, and keyboardist Gillian Gilbert's accidental inclusion of an extra rest in her handwritten notation was deliberately kept for the added tension it brought to the arrangement. "He built a sequencer that could be connected to the band's new sampler, a keyboard called an emulator. They sampled a choral effect from a craftwork song called Uranium and wrote a bass line using another keyboard called a Mogue source."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the Drum Machine

xref.title: Chowder's Post-Band Career
xref.body: Bass player "Chowder" later worked with Moist and David Usher. He now works at a BMW motorcycle shop and occasionally performs at quiet, anonymous gigs and open mics, indicating a partial return to music. "Chowder, the bass player, later worked with Moist and David Usher, now works at BMW in the motorcycle shop and still plays the odd time."

xref.title: David Usher's Solo Career
xref.body: During Moist's 12-year break, singer David Usher embarked on a successful solo career, releasing seven albums independently. This allowed him to maintain a strong musical presence outside of the band. "Singer David Usher went solo releasing seven albums on his own."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Engineer for "Blue Monday"
xref.body: Engineer Martin Usher was brought in by New Order to write the necessary code that enabled all the different electronic devices used in the creation of "Blue Monday" to communicate and synchronize with each other. "An engineer named Martin Usher was brought in and he wrote some code that got all the different devices talking to each other."

xref.title: Kingston Roots and Connection to Hugh Dillon
xref.body: The members of The Tragically Hip grew up in Kingston and attended the same high school as Hugh Dillon, maintaining a kind relationship with him during his tumultuous youth. "I grew up in Kingston with David Usher and the guys in the hip. We all went to the same high school."

xref.title: Kingston Upbringing and Early Connections
xref.body: Grew up in Kingston, attending high school with Hugh Dillon. He was the frontman for his first band, The Slinks, and later became the iconic singer of The Tragically Hip. "I grew up in Kingston with David Usher and the guys in the hip. We all went to the same high school."

xref.title: Kingston Upbringing and Early Influences
xref.body: Grew up in Kingston, sharing high school with future members of The Tragically Hip and David Usher. He struggled academically but was intensely drawn to rock and roll, absorbing music from his older siblings and becoming a huge Bob Dylan fan. "I remember being 18 and I grew up in Kingston with David Usher and the guys in the hip. We all went to the same high school."
